Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit; leaves may curl and drop early.
Apple___Apple_scab.causes: Fungus Venturia inaequalis, spread by wind and rain in cool, wet spring weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.cures: Remove fallen leaves, prune for airflow, apply fungicide (captan or myclobutanil) starting at bud break.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple spots on leaves, brown rotting fruit with concentric rings, sunken cankers on bark.
Apple___Black_rot.causes: Fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa, entering through wounds and spreading in warm, humid conditions.
Apple___Black_rot.cures: Prune out dead wood and mummified fruit, apply fungicide sprays, keep trees healthy and well-watered.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on leaves, sometimes with tube-like structures underneath.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.causes: Fungus Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae, requiring nearby juniper/cedar trees to complete its cycle.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cures: Remove nearby juniper hosts if possible, apply preventive fungicide in spring, plant resistant varieties.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: No visible spots, discoloration, or lesions; leaves are uniformly green.
Apple___healthy.cures: Maintain good watering, pruning, and periodic monitoring to keep the tree disease-free.

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are green and uniform with no spotting or wilting.
Blueberry___healthy.cures: Continue balanced fertilization, proper spacing, and regular inspection.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves and shoots, leaf curling, stunted new growth.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.causes: Fungus Podosphaera clandestina, favored by warm days, cool nights, and poor air circulation.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.cures: Prune for airflow, avoid excess nitrogen, apply sulfur or potassium bicarbonate fungicide.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: No white coating, spots, or curling; leaves appear normal and green.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.cures: Maintain regular pruning and monitoring to sustain plant health.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Rectangular gray-tan lesions running parallel to leaf veins, eventually merging and killing leaf tissue.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.causes: Fungus Cercospora zeae-maydis, thriving in humid, warm weather with extended leaf wetness.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.cures: Rotate crops, use resistant hybrids, apply foliar fungicide if disease pressure is high.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small reddish-brown raised pustules scattered on both leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.causes: Fungus Puccinia sorghi, spread by windborne spores, favored by cool, moist conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.cures: Plant resistant hybrids, apply fungicide if severe, avoid excessive overhead irrigation.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical grayish-green to tan lesions on leaves, resembling cigar shapes.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.causes: Fungus Exserohilum turcicum, spread by wind and rain, favored by moderate temperatures and humidity.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cures: Use resistant hybrids, rotate crops, till residue, apply fungicide during early infection.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are green and free of lesions or discoloration.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.cures: Continue crop rotation and regular field monitoring.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Small brown circular spots on leaves, shriveled black 'mummified' berries.
Grape___Black_rot.causes: Fungus Guignardia bidwellii, spreading in warm, wet spring and summer conditions.
Grape___Black_rot.cures: Remove mummified berries and infected debris, apply fungicide from early spring through veraison.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe pattern of yellow and brown streaks between leaf veins, dark spotted berries.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).causes: Complex of wood-rotting fungi entering through pruning wounds, worsened by stress and age.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).cures: No full cure; prune out infected wood, avoid large pruning wounds, protect cuts with sealant.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots on leaves that enlarge and cause premature leaf drop.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.causes: Fungus Pseudocercospora vitis, favored by warm, humid, rainy conditions.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.cures: Improve canopy airflow, remove infected leaves, apply copper-based or other fungicide.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Leaves and fruit show no spots, discoloration, or unusual patterns.
Grape___healthy.cures: Maintain routine canopy management and disease monitoring.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy yellow mottling on leaves, lopsided bitter fruit, twig dieback.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).causes: Bacterium spread by the Asian citrus psyllid insect; no known cure once infected.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cures: Remove and destroy infected trees, control psyllid populations, plant certified disease-free stock.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit that may crack and form scabs.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.causes: Bacterium Xanthomonas campestris pv. pruni, spread by rain splash and wind in warm weather.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.cures: Plant resistant varieties, apply copper-based bactericide, avoid overhead irrigation.

Peach___healthy.symptoms: Leaves and fruit are free of spots or lesions.
Peach___healthy.cures: Continue regular pruning, watering, and monitoring.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown with yellow halos, spots also on fruit.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.causes: Bacterium Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria, spread by rain splash and contaminated tools.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.cures: Use disease-free seed, rotate crops, apply copper-based bactericide, avoid overhead watering.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Leaves and fruit appear normal with no spotting.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.cures: Maintain balanced watering and periodic inspection.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings ('target' pattern) on older leaves first.
Potato___Early_blight.causes: Fungus Alternaria solani, favored by warm temperatures and alternating wet/dry conditions.
Potato___Early_blight.cures: Rotate crops, remove infected debris, apply fungicide such as chlorothalonil or mancozeb.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked gray-green spots on leaves turning brown/black, white mold on leaf undersides.
Potato___Late_blight.causes: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans, spreading rapidly in cool, wet, humid weather.
Potato___Late_blight.cures: Destroy infected plants promptly, apply fungicide preventively, avoid overhead irrigation.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Leaves show no spots, wilting, or discoloration.
Potato___healthy.cures: Continue crop rotation and regular field checks.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Leaves and canes appear normal with no lesions or discoloration.
Raspberry___healthy.cures: Maintain proper pruning and spacing for airflow.

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are uniformly green with no spots or curling.
Soybean___healthy.cures: Continue crop rotation and routine field monitoring.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on leaves and stems, leaves may yellow and shrivel.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.causes: Fungus Podosphaera xanthii, favored by warm days, high humidity, and shaded conditions.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.cures: Improve air circulation, remove infected leaves, apply sulfur or potassium bicarbonate spray.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Small purple spots on leaves that merge into scorched-looking brown patches.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.causes: Fungus Diplocarpon earlianum, spread by rain splash in warm, wet conditions.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.cures: Remove infected leaves after harvest, improve airflow, apply fungicide if recurring.

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are green and free from spotting or scorching.
Strawberry___healthy.cures: Maintain proper spacing, mulching, and regular monitoring.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit turning dark brown with yellow halos.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.causes: Xanthomonas bacteria, spread by rain splash, handling, and contaminated seed.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cures: Use certified disease-free seed, rotate crops, apply copper-based bactericide.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings on lower leaves first, yellowing around lesions.
Tomato___Early_blight.causes: Fungus Alternaria solani, favored by warm temperatures and humid conditions.
Tomato___Early_blight.cures: Remove infected lower leaves, mulch soil, apply fungicide like chlorothalonil.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large water-soaked gray-green blotches on leaves, white fungal growth on undersides.
Tomato___Late_blight.causes: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans, spreading fast in cool, wet, humid weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.cures: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately, apply preventive fungicide, avoid wet foliage.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow spots on upper leaf surface, olive-green to gray mold underneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.causes: Fungus Passalora fulva, favored by high humidity and poor ventilation, common in greenhouses.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.cures: Improve ventilation, reduce humidity, remove infected leaves, apply fungicide if needed.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small circular spots with dark borders and gray centers, mainly on lower leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.causes: Fungus Septoria lycopersici, spread by rain splash in warm, humid conditions.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.cures: Remove infected leaves, mulch to prevent soil splash, apply fungicide, rotate crops.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling on leaves, fine webbing, leaves may bronze and dry out.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.causes: Tetranychus urticae mites, thriving in hot, dry conditions with low humidity.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.cures: Spray leaves with water to disrupt mites, use insecticidal soap or miticide, introduce predatory mites.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown lesions with concentric rings on leaves, stems, and fruit.
Tomato___Target_Spot.causes: Fungus Corynespora cassiicola, favored by warm, humid, and wet conditions.
Tomato___Target_Spot.cures: Remove infected debris, improve airflow, apply fungicide, avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of leaves, stunted growth, reduced fruit set.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.causes: Virus transmitted by whiteflies; no cure once a plant is infected.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cures: Remove and destroy infected plants, control whiteflies, use resistant varieties and row covers.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green pattern on leaves, leaf curling, stunted growth.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.causes: Virus spread by contaminated hands, tools, and seed; no cure once infected.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cures: Remove and destroy infected plants, disinfect tools, use resistant varieties and certified seed.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Leaves and fruit appear normal with no discoloration or lesions.
Tomato___healthy.cures: Continue balanced watering, staking, and regular inspection.
